label: bug
file: src/components/ExportButton.tsx

handleClick's promise chain only has a success path: exportReport(...).then(() => { setBusy(false); ... }) with no .catch/.finally. When the fetch fails or exportReport rejects (e.g. a non-2xx response throws), setBusy(false) never runs, so `busy` stays true and the button (and format select) remain disabled until the page is reloaded. Fix by resetting `busy` in a .finally() (and surfacing an error toast on rejection) so the button re-enables after a failed export.

input.title: Re-enable the export button after a failed export
input.body:
File: src/components/ExportButton.tsx

In `handleClick`, `exportReport(...)` is called with only a `.then()` handler, so `setBusy(false)` only runs when the export succeeds. When the fetch rejects or `exportReport` throws (non-2xx response, network error), the promise rejection is unhandled and `busy` stays `true` forever, leaving the button greyed out until the page is reloaded.

Add a failure path that also clears the busy state, e.g. a `.catch()` (or try/finally with async/await) that calls `setBusy(false)` and shows an error toast, so a failed export leaves the button usable again instead of stuck disabled.
